subject: Conditional EU data residency and temporary cross-region processing authorization
messages:
From: MedBridge DPO <dpo@medbridge.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: MedBridge Legal <legal@medbridge.com>, procurement@medbridge.com
Date: 2027-04-01T09:18:00Z
Subject: EU residency confirmation + temporary DR processing window

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the call this morning. As part of our procurement and DPA review we need clear commitments on two points before we can move to signature:

1) A firm statement of EU data residency for MedBridge production data (including embeddings and logs) and whether KMS keys ever leave the EU.
2) If Redwood anticipates any temporary cross-region processing (e.g., for DR, cache synchronization, or model warm-up), please describe the policy, maximum duration of any transient copies outside the EU, and the controls to limit exposure.

We also need the subprocessor roster that will process MedBridge data and an outline of the deletion/notification process after any transient processing event.

Can you provide a DPA addendum draft that includes: conditional egress language, maximum window for transient processing, required notifications, and audit log retention commitments? We prefer the tightest possible windows (24 hours preferred) but are willing to evaluate a case for longer windows for critical DR events.

Attachment: MedBridge-residency-Q.docx (questions)

Best,
Ari Green
DPO, MedBridge Health

--
MedBridge Health
Data Protection Office
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Ari Green <dpo@medbridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T12:04:00Z
Subject: Re: EU residency confirmation + temporary DR processing window

Ari —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, details below and a draft addendum attached.

- Residency: Production customer data (payloads, embeddings, per-request metadata) for an EU tenant will be served from EU-only infrastructure; we provide region pinning so that normal inference traffic remains in-region.
- KMS: Customer-managed keys (BYOK) are supported; if you bring an EU KMS key it never leaves the EU. For Redwood-managed keys we currently store master key material in the region specified for the tenant (EU) and do not export keys for routine syncs — only cryptographic references are used for cross-region failover under controls.
- Transient processing: We propose a default conditional egress policy with a 48-hour maximum transient window for defined DR or capacity overflow events, extendable to 72 hours with pre-approval and documented rationale. We can tighten to 24 hours in the addendum if MedBridge requires that as a default.

Controls we propose to include in the addendum:
- Explicit event types that qualify (DR, warm-up, urgent patching) and an approval process.
- Ephemeral cache TTLs (default 24 hours) and guaranteed deletion of KV caches and temporary copies within the window.
- KMS protections: regional master keys (no export), ephemeral session keys for cross-region sessions, and signed attestations if keys are rotated.
- Auditability: event notification within 2 hours of transient processing start, full audit trail delivered via secure share, and retention of those logs for 90 days (extendable on request).

I'm attaching a draft addendum that tracks these items (draft-eu-egress-addendum-v1.pdf) and a current subprocessor roster snapshot (subprocessor_roster_20270401.csv).

Next steps I propose:
1) Legal teams review addendum (we can accept redlines).
2) Procurement confirms any SOW/pricing impact for dedicated pinning/DR guarantees.
3) If agreed, final DocuSign routing (we can do an embedded signing link).

Attachment: draft-eu-egress-addendum-v1.pdf (stub)
Attachment: subprocessor_roster_20270401.csv (stub)

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ari Green <dpo@medbridge.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-02T08:33:00Z
Subject: Re: EU residency confirmation + temporary DR processing window

Ari / Naomi —

Couple procurement notes from our side:

- If MedBridge requires a contractual default of 24-hour maximum transient egress (rather than a higher default with case-by-case extensions), this is treated as a residual risk reduction and does not change base pricing for hosted tenants; however, for Dedicated/Reserved capacity with SLA-backed pinning and guaranteed hardware residency we will need a capacity commitment (we can provide T-shirt sizing).
- We typically attach a short SOW clause for guaranteed proof-of-activation (time-stamped logs) and an annual attestation. Adding a 24-hour deletion guarantee for caches/log copies is acceptable; proof-of-deletion artifacts will be provided as part of the incident packet.
- For subprocessors: we can include a clause that Redwood will not add new subprocessors for EU processing without 30 days' notice and a mechanism for escrowed names if a non-standard vendor is required for DR.

I ran this by Karthik (ops) — he confirms we can enforce ephemeral cache TTLs and produce deletion certificates; for KMS, if you provide BYOK we will not export key material.

Suggested timeline: legal redlines returned within 7 business days, procurement SOW discussion in parallel, final sign-off target within two weeks if there are no major redlines.

Attachment: procurement-pin-options.pdf (pricing sketch)

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Contracts, Redwood Inference
From: MedBridge DPO <dpo@medbridge.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, MedBridge Legal <legal@medbridge.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T14:10:00Z
Subject: Re: EU residency confirmation + temporary DR processing window

Naomi / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the draft addendum. Our legal team reviewed and proposed a few redlines to tighten controls:

- Default transient egress window: please change to 24 hours unless an explicitly documented DR declaration is made by both parties; for DR declarations, allow up to 72 hours with written notice and post-event justification.
- KMS: we require a guarantee that customer-provided EU keys (BYOK) will not be exported or backed up outside the EU; any use of Redwood-managed keys for EU tenants must be disclosed and require customer consent.
- Notification: please commit to an automated notification within one hour of any transient processing start and provide a full incident packet within 48 hours with deletion proofs.
- Audit logs: 180 days retention for MedBridge-specific transient-processing logs.

We are OK with the 30-day notice for adding subprocessors but request a carve-out for emergency subcontracting only with prior written consent (i.e., not unilateral).

Please incorporate these redlines into draft-eu-egress-addendum-v2 and send back with a proposed DocuSign routing link. We will route internally for sign-off upon receiving v2.

Regards,
Ari Green
DPO, MedBridge Health
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>

Ari —

Appreciate the clear redlines. We have accepted the core tightening items and prepared v2 with your language. Summary of changes we accepted:

- Default transient egress window set to 24 hours; DR declarations allow up to 72 hours with signed dual-party declaration.
- Strong BYOK guarantee: customer-provided EU keys will not be exported; Redwood-managed keys will only be used with explicit customer consent and documented in the tenant's security profile.
- Notification: automated start notice within 1 hour, incident packet within 48 hours.
- Audit retention: adjusted to 180 days for MedBridge transient-processing logs.
- Subprocessors: 30-day notice remains; emergency subcontracting allowed only with prior written consent (no unilateral emergency borrowing).

I have uploaded the redlined addendum and a DocuSign embedded signing link here: https://redwood-share.example.com/drive/MedBridge-eu-addendum-draft and https://docusign.example.com/embeddedSigning/abcdef123456.
